docs.title: Workspace
docs.text:
A workspace gives a team a place to keep data, run code, and share results. Members use shared object storage and services, with browser sessions for their code. They can grant another workspace access to a bucket or publish files for anyone to download.

Open a Datalab session for its editor and terminal. Use its Data tab to browse storage with PackageR. A permanent Data address lets people read and download published results even when compute sessions are stopped.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
Follow the quickstart to create a test workspace, publish satellite images, and read them through public links and S3 clients. The STAC registration example has three flows: publish with Portolan and demonstrate search; copy assets to the public folder in the same workspace bucket with stacpkg relocation and share the catalogue; then deploy a second API from an OCI metadata package by digest.

Use the notebook guide to choose an example and check what it needs before you run it.

For an existing workspace, use Concepts to add a colleague, share a bucket with another team, publish a dataset, or start a session.

docs.title: Set up the service
docs.text:
Operators can use installation to set up the shared services. Use IAM integration to give people and jobs the access they need, and operational controls to set session resources and network access.

The architecture page shows how the API, Crossplane packages, and runtime services fit together.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
Use workspace storage to keep a team’s datasets in one place. Add members to work with those files, grant another workspace access to a bucket, or publish results for readers without an account. Sessions and managed services give the team tools to process that data.

Open your workspace dashboard and select Management to manage members, buckets, sessions, and services. The available tabs and actions depend on your workspace role.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
A Storage resource defines buckets, a storage identity, access requests, grants, and lifecycle rules. Workspace members use that identity and its bucket permissions. A bucket grant lets another workspace use selected data with its own credentials, so teams can share a dataset without copying it.

A discoverable bucket can appear in another workspace’s access-request list. Its owner still has to approve access. The receiving workspace then uses its own storage credentials to reach the bucket.

Permission Access ReadOnly List and read objects. ReadWrite List, read, write, and delete objects. WriteOnly List, write, and delete objects, without reading their contents. None Record that access is not granted.

For manifest-based setup, backends that resolve requests from peer Storage resources also need storages.pkg.internal/discoverable: "true" on the owner resource. The per-bucket discoverable field advertises the bucket; it is not a storage policy.

Lifecycle rules belong to spec.buckets[].lifecycleRules. A rule selects the whole bucket with * or a prefix such as tmp/*. Notify reports matching objects; Delete removes them. Set exactly one age (minAge, such as 12h) or UTC cutoff (at).

See the provider’s permission model for backend details.

docs.title: Create a bucket
docs.text:
Open Buckets, add a unique bucket name, and save it. Start the name with your workspace name, for example ws-test-20261024071434-test. Wait for storage to finish creating the bucket before uploading files.

Mark a bucket as discoverable to let other workspaces find it and request access. This does not make its objects public. See public shares for public downloads.

docs.title: Share a bucket with another workspace
docs.text:
1. In the receiving workspace, request access to the owner’s discoverable bucket.
  2. In the owner’s workspace, open Requested Buckets, review the permission, and select Grant bucket access.
  3. Wait for the storage policy to update.
  4. In the receiving workspace, use its existing storage credentials to access the shared bucket.

Use ReadOnly for a reader. The permission table describes each level.

docs.title: Datalabs and sessions
docs.text:
A Datalab resource defines the team’s users, sessions, and shared services. Start a session when you need an editor, a terminal, or a place to run code. Each named session has a persistent home volume, so you can stop it and keep your files for the next run.

Sessions share the workspace’s storage identity and managed services. A session can use a host-cluster namespace or its own virtual Kubernetes control plane. See operational controls for the settings.

docs.title: Start or stop a session
docs.text:
Open Sessions to add a named session or change its state. Opening its Datalab link starts a stopped session when the API supports on-demand access.

Shared storage, Data, and managed databases have separate lifecycles. See session controls for the initial mode and storage limits.

docs.title: Managed services
docs.text: Use a managed service when your code needs a database, cache, or vector store shared within the workspace. PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Qdrant need their operators installed in the platform. A registry can store container images and OCI packages for use by session workloads.

docs.title: Add a managed service
docs.text:
Use Stores to request an available service. The platform operator must install and configure its database operator first.

An operator can also add a service to the existing Datalab configuration. For example, this block requests a MongoDB store named test:

spec:
  documentStores:
    test:
      storage: 1Gi

Keep the Datalab’s other fields when adding this block. The session receives MONGO_TEST_URI after the service is ready. Stop and start the session to load changed connection settings.

Provider Datalab’s usage guide describes the PostgreSQL, cache, vector, and registry fields. Its application examples cover tools such as MLflow.

docs.title: Data access and sharing
docs.text:
PackageR is the workspace storage browser. The Data service is enabled by default. An operator can give it a permanent address such as https://<workspace-name>.lab.example.org. The Datalab’s Data tab opens that same service.

With a permanent address, storage browsing and public shares work without a running compute session. Sign in to browse private workspace data. A public share or presigned download link can be used without a workspace account.

docs.title: Public shares
docs.text:
Put files in the public/ folder of the bucket named after the workspace. For ws-bob, this is s3://ws-bob/public/. The default share exposes that folder for public browsing and downloads. A public/ folder in another bucket is not shared automatically.

Open /share/public/ on the Data hostname. Every file placed in this folder is public. Upload files through PackageR when writes are allowed, or use the backing storage endpoint and its credentials.

docs.title: Presigned download links
docs.text:
A presigned URL gives temporary access to one object. In PackageR, select a file, open Info, then select Show beside Presigned URL.

This URL points to object storage. It works until it expires, and the recipient needs network access to that storage endpoint.

A public-share download route can redirect to a fresh presigned URL. Share that route when you need a link that lasts longer than one signed URL. Workspace Management checks both download paths against the uploaded bytes.

docs.title: STAC catalogues
docs.text:
Use STAC to describe when data was collected, which area it covers, and where to download its files. Applications can read these descriptions to choose the data they need.

Put a STAC GeoParquet file at public/catalog.parquet to publish a catalogue through the existing Data service. PackageR reads it when someone requests the catalogue and builds Collection and Item responses with public asset links. Relative asset paths resolve within the share folder.

Start with the Vienna notebook to publish satellite images and let other people download them. It crops three images, adds descriptions for the cropped area, and checks public and authenticated S3 downloads.

The registration notebook has three flows. Flow 1 uploads with Portolan under published/ and demonstrates API search. Flow 2 uses stacpkg relocation to copy the assets under public/ in the same workspace bucket. The source files stay in place. PackageR serves the public catalogue through the existing Data service, with HTTP asset links for browser access. Flow 3 pushes a metadata package to the workspace OCI container registry as an artifact. A second API reads the package by digest, so a team can deploy the same catalogue again. The notebook guide compares these views and their setup.

docs.title: S3 clients
docs.text:
The optional Data S3 endpoint lets AWS tools read data through the Data hostname. It uses path-style requests, and is read only. Uploads use the backing object-storage endpoint.

Signing setting Value Endpoint The workspace’s permanent Data URL. Access key ID The workspace name. Secret access key The same workspace name. Session token A valid Keycloak access token.

The signing names are public identifiers. The token must include the workspace name in aud and ws_access, ws_admin, or ws_api under that workspace’s client roles. Human users can use device login through the central client. A service can use the generated workspace client’s credentials.

The endpoint supports bucket and object listing, HEAD, GET, and byte-range GET. It rejects uploads and S3 query-presigned requests. S3 reads of public/ objects still need a token; public-share links use a separate route.

Operators enable S3 through the Gateway settings. The Vienna notebook refreshes its device login before the S3 and AWS CLI steps and checks the downloaded files by SHA-256.

docs.title: Automatic token renewal
docs.text:
For service access, use scripts/s3-credentials.py as an AWS credential_process. The script returns the signing values, an OAuth access token, and its expiry time. AWS CLI and Boto3 can run it again when they need fresh credentials. See the AWS process credential documentation.

Run these commands from the repository root. Install Python and AWS CLI first. Replace the workspace name, Data URL, and Keycloak realm URL with your service settings. The workspace OAuth client must have the audience and role described above.

aws configure set region us-east-1 --profile ws-alice
aws configure set endpoint_url https://ws-alice.lab.example.org --profile ws-alice
aws configure set s3.addressing_style path --profile ws-alice
aws configure set credential_process \
  "python3 \"$PWD/scripts/s3-credentials.py\" --tenant ws-alice --issuer https://keycloak.example.org/realms/eoepca" \
  --profile ws-alice

These commands add a profile to ~/.aws/config. The process command uses the script’s absolute path. It belongs in the config file; do not copy the returned token into ~/.aws/credentials. The resulting profile has this form:

[profile ws-alice]
region = us-east-1
endpoint_url = https://ws-alice.lab.example.org
credential_process = python3 "/absolute/path/to/workspace/scripts/s3-credentials.py" --tenant ws-alice --issuer https://keycloak.example.org/realms/eoepca
s3 =
    addressing_style = path

Enter the OAuth client secret once for the current terminal. The hidden prompt keeps it out of shell history. The helper reads CLIENT_SECRET when AWS starts it.

CLIENT_SECRET="$(python3 -c 'import getpass; print(getpass.getpass("OAuth client secret: "))')"
export CLIENT_SECRET
unset AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
aws s3 ls s3://ws-alice/ --profile ws-alice

Boto3 can use the same profile from a process started in that terminal:

import boto3

session = boto3.Session(profile_name="ws-alice")
s3 = session.client("s3")
objects = s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket="ws-alice", MaxKeys=10)

Keep CLIENT_SECRET available while these clients run so the helper can get new tokens. Run unset CLIENT_SECRET when you finish. This profile provides read-only access through the Data endpoint. Use the registration notebook for uploads to backing storage.

docs.title: Membership
docs.text:
Add members so colleagues can use the workspace’s data and services. A workspace role controls dashboard and management actions. Members who can view storage credentials use the workspace’s full storage policy, including its existing bucket grants.

The owner of another workspace approves any additional bucket grant. See IAM roles for the management permissions.

docs.title: Add a member
docs.text:
1. Open Members.
  2. Add an existing Keycloak username and select its workspace role.
  3. Save the change.
  4. Ask the new member to sign in again to load the assigned roles.

Give workspace administrator access to people who need to manage members, buckets, sessions, or stores.

docs.title: Check a workspace that is still starting
docs.text:
An operator can inspect status without reading credential values:

kubectl get storage,datalab -n workspace
workspace_name=ws-test-20261024071434
kubectl describe datalab "$workspace_name" -n workspace

Set workspace_name to the name printed by your notebook. Check the reported conditions and events. If storage works but the Data hostname does not, check its workload, HTTPRoute, Gateway listener, certificate reference, DNS, and public load-balancer route.

docs.title: Workspace Management¶
docs.text:
Create a test workspace for a user, upload one sample preview image, and share them without giving recipients workspace credentials.

The notebook uses separate administrator and owner logins. It checks that temporary S3 downloads and permanent public-share downloads return the same bytes as the uploads.

docs.title: Run the notebook¶
docs.text:
From the repository root:

uv sync
uv run jupyter lab docs/workspace-management.ipynb

The checkout includes notebook_support.py, eoepca-demo.env, and the three-Item sample docs/catalog.v1.parquet. Keep the helper beside this notebook. The settings file contains public service URLs and OAuth settings; user tokens stay in kernel memory.

The sample items point to preview and thumbnail assets. You can use another STAC GeoParquet file with those asset keys.

docs.title: 1. Load the service settings¶
docs.text:
The central public client workspace-api needs S256 PKCE and Device Authorization Grant enabled. Set WORKSPACE_CLIENT_ID to that client in the settings file.

Load the settings and check the service addresses:

docs.title: 2. Sign in as the owner and creator¶
docs.text:
Enter alice, bob, or eric as the owner and complete device login as that user.

If the owner cannot create workspaces, sign in as oscar when prompted. Use a fresh private browser window for each account. See roles for the required access.

docs.title: 3. Create a test workspace¶
docs.text:
The workspace name is ws-test-<UTC timestamp>. The API adds the ws- prefix.

The creator signs in as a platform administrator. The owner uses the storage and sharing steps.

docs.title: 4. Open the owner's workspace¶
docs.text:
Refresh the owner's login to load the new workspace roles. Open the displayed links as the owner. The dashboard starts sessions; the management page edits members and bucket access.

The following steps use the owner's storage credentials.

docs.title: 5. Upload one sample via S3¶
docs.text: Upload catalog.v1.parquet via backing S3, then copy one preview from its first Item into workspace storage.

docs.title: 6. Check a temporary download¶
docs.text:
Generate one presigned URL with the S3 client. Download the sample from backing object storage, compare its checksum, and display it. Print the full URL, which expires after 15 minutes.

This cell signs the URL locally with boto3. Step 7 shows the PackageR HTTP API that returns a presigned URL in JSON.

docs.title: 7. Check a public download via the PackageR HTTP API¶
docs.text:
Copy the sample via backing S3 into public/. Anyone with its public-share link can read it.

To get a presigned URL in a JSON response, call:

GET <Data URL>/api/public/share/public/<filename>?presign=true

Read the presignedURL field. To get an HTTP redirect to that URL instead, add &followRedirect=true. The client follows the redirect and downloads the bytes from object storage. The permanent PackageR link can issue a new signed URL when the old one expires.

docs.title: Result¶
docs.text:
The owner has workspace storage and two ways to share verified images: an expiring object-storage link and a permanent public-share route. The workspace and uploaded files stay available.

Use the printed workspace name in the other notebooks.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
A workspace brings together a team’s storage, access roles, sessions, and shared services. Users request these through the Workspace API. They can keep published data available while compute sessions are stopped.

The API records the requested configuration as Storage and Datalab resources in Kubernetes. Crossplane runs their compositions to create and update storage, identity resources, sessions, and services. The diagram shows which component handles each part of a workspace request.

flowchart TD
    UI[Workspace dashboard and management] --> API[Workspace API]
    API --> S[Storage resource]
    API --> D[Datalab resource]
    S --> PS[Provider Storage]
    PS --> B[S3 buckets and storage identities]
    D --> PD[Provider Datalab]
    PD --> IAM[Keycloak clients, groups, and roles]
    PD --> DATA[Shared Data service]
    PD --> SESSION[Named Datalab sessions]
    PD --> STORES[Optional managed stores]

docs.title: Storage and runtime
docs.text:
Provider Storage creates buckets, storage identities, policies, and credential Secrets. Backend compositions support MinIO, AWS S3, OTC OBS, OVHcloud, and CloudFerro.

Provider Datalab uses those storage credentials. It creates the shared Data service, requested stores, and the declared sessions. A session has its own home volume and can have a virtual Kubernetes control plane. Shared Data and managed stores can run while sessions are stopped.

The API and UI run as separate components from the composition packages. The pipeline chart installs the Storage and Datalab packages and their shared configuration. It does not deploy the Workspace API or UI.

docs.title: Shared configuration
docs.text:
Use an EnvironmentConfig to apply common platform settings to workspaces. It holds the domain, IAM, storage, network, and default resource settings used by the compositions. A resource selects it with its environment annotation or label.

The pipeline chart creates one EnvironmentConfig, named datalab by default. Educates has separate installation values for the session ingress domain, class, and TLS Secret. Those values must match the Datalab environment settings. See installation.

Crossplane updates resources from the declared configuration. An operator can use GitOps or the Workspace API to manage that configuration. Assign each field to one writer so the API and GitOps do not replace each other’s changes.

docs.title: Request paths
docs.text:
The platform gateway protects the Workspace API and browser session routes. The permanent Data endpoint has its own OAuth protection. Public shares and authenticated Data S3 reads use separate routes on the Data hostname.

Workloads created inside a vCluster still run on the host cluster. The host controls their network access, admission rules, and public routes. IAM integration describes token checks; operational controls describes the Workspace settings.

docs.title: IAM integration
docs.text: People need to sign in to manage a workspace. Jobs need access that works without a person at a browser. Keycloak provides both user tokens and service-account tokens; workspace roles determine which API actions each caller can use. Storage policies control S3 object access.

docs.title: Login and workspace clients
docs.text:
Use a central public client, such as workspace-api, for user login to the API, UI, and shared session routes. For Workspace Management and the Vienna notebook, enable Device Authorization Grant and S256 PKCE on this client. A user signs in once and receives the roles for their workspaces.

Provider Datalab creates a separate confidential client for each workspace. Its ID matches the Datalab name. It enables service accounts and browser login, limits role scope, and disables implicit, password, and device grants.

Resource Example Use Central public client workspace-api Browser and device login for people. Workspace confidential client ws-alice Workspace roles and machine tokens. User group ws-alice Assign ws_access. Admin group ws-alice-admin Assign ws_admin. Runtime Secret ws-alice-oauth2-client Supply client_id and client_secret to services.

The runtime Secret is a machine credential. A caller who can read it can request a service-account token for that workspace. The STAC registration notebook uses client credentials to show how an upload can run without user login.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Workspace API access ws_access View storage credentials, members, buckets, resource usage, stores, and sessions. ws_admin All user actions; manage members, buckets, stores, and sessions; request machine tokens. ws_api View workspace storage credentials. Assigned to the workspace client service account. admin on workspace-api Platform administration across workspaces, including workspace creation.

The resource-usage permission is VIEW_RESOURCE_USAGE. The machine-token permission is ISSUE_TOKENS; ws_admin includes both. The service-account role ws_api cannot manage a workspace or open interactive browser routes.

A workspace role limits management actions. Members with access to the shared storage credentials use the same storage policy. Bucket grants control which other workspace buckets that identity can use.

docs.title: Token claims
docs.text:
The gateway checks the token signature, issuer, expiry, audience, and route policy. The Workspace API reads the validated bearer token:

  • aud includes the API audience, normally workspace-api.
  • preferred_username identifies the caller.
  • resource_access.<workspace>.roles holds the workspace roles.
  • resource_access.workspace-api.roles can hold the platform admin role.

This example gives Alice user access to one workspace and administrator access to another:

{
  "aud": ["workspace-api"],
  "azp": "workspace-api",
  "preferred_username": "alice",
  "resource_access": {
    "ws-alice": {"roles": ["ws_access"]},
    "ws-bob": {"roles": ["ws_admin"]}
  }
}

For generated workspace clients, add the API audience through EnvironmentConfig.data.iam.extraAudiences. Configure the central user client to emit the required audiences and workspace roles as well. Refresh a user token after a new workspace or membership is created.

The Data S3 endpoint also requires the workspace name in aud. See S3 clients for its signing values.

docs.title: Machine access
docs.text:
A client-credentials token identifies the workspace service account. It has ws_api under the workspace client roles and a username such as service-account-ws-alice.

Use OAuth client credentials for a scheduled upload or a task delegated to another service. The job requests a token with its client ID and secret, calls the Workspace API for storage credentials, and passes those credentials to its upload tool. No workspace team member needs to be present or sign in through a browser. The token needs the API audience and the target workspace’s ws_api role.

The STAC registration notebook uses this path for Portolan uploads and stacpkg relocation. The first API’s startup Secret supplies storage access until it switches to public HTTP metadata. For a job, replace the prompts with job settings and a client secret from its secret store. OCI publishing uses separate registry credentials.

The API also has /workspaces/<workspace-name>/token for callers with ISSUE_TOKENS or platform administration. That route returns a workspace machine token. It does not replace user login.

docs.title: Route protection
docs.text:
Protect the shared UI and session routes with the workspace roles in resource_access. A service owned by one workspace can use its confidential client and require the expected audience, client ID, and roles.

Provider Datalab supplies OAuth protection for the permanent Data browser. Public-share routes allow anonymous downloads. The read-only Data S3 endpoint validates its own signed requests and bearer tokens. Configure the Data issuer URLs in the installation values.

docs.title: Operational controls
docs.text: Use these settings to choose when sessions start, how much storage and memory they can request, and which services they can reach. The platform operator manages the host cluster, public routing, and storage services.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
Choose whether a new workspace starts a session immediately, starts one when a user opens it, or has no default session. The Workspace API’s SESSION_MODE sets this initial state:

Value Initial state auto Declare default as stopped; opening its Datalab link starts it. on Declare default as started. off Do not declare a default session.

Automatic shutdown needs an operator job or policy. The API does not stop idle sessions by itself.

A stopped session keeps its home PVC. Object storage and shared Data or database services have separate lifecycles. Set spec.quota for session memory, volume size, and budget. spec.overallQuota.storage limits requested PVC storage in the Datalab environment namespace; it does not cover object storage or PVCs in other namespaces.

docs.title: Kubernetes access
docs.text:
Namespace mode uses the host control plane and a session namespace role. In vCluster mode, each started session gets a virtual Kubernetes control plane. Its workloads still use host-cluster nodes and remain subject to host policies.

Use spec.security to select the Pod security level, Kubernetes token access, namespace role, and external egress. Omitted fields use EnvironmentConfig.data.defaults.security, then provider defaults. Configure the host’s admission policies and resource limits separately.

docs.title: Network access
docs.text:
Allow the connections that session code needs, such as HTTPS to a data provider or access to platform storage. The network plugin must enforce Kubernetes NetworkPolicy. Policies add their allowed connections together.

Generated policy Created when Allows deny-egress By default No outbound traffic on its own. allow-namespace-egress By default Pods in the same runtime namespace. allow-vcluster-egress vCluster is enabled The session’s virtual API. allow-dns-egress External egress, vCluster, or Data is enabled Cluster DNS. allow-external-egress External egress is enabled and external CIDRs are set The configured external CIDRs, with exclusions. allow-internal-egress Valid network.internalEgress entries exist Selected Pods and ports in other namespaces.

The per-Datalab spec.security.externalEgress setting overrides the environment default. An empty external CIDR list creates no broad external allow rule.

Set the cluster Service and Pod CIDRs and any blocked ranges in the EnvironmentConfig. The provider excludes them from broad external rules. Use network.internalEgress for selected storage, identity, and other platform services.

network.excludePolicies can omit generated policies by name. Data services also have their own policies. Check the policies actually installed in each namespace when testing a connection.

docs.title: Data and public routes
docs.text:
Use a permanent Data address for downloads that must stay available when a compute session stops. spec.data.enabled defaults to true and cannot change after Datalab creation. Set it when creating the resource. spec.data.readOnlyMount controls Data browser permissions; storage IAM still controls object access. The optional Data S3 endpoint is always read only.

Manage public routes in the host cluster. For a permanent Data address, the public load balancer must reach the selected Gateway listener, and that listener must terminate TLS. Storage can be ready before the Data workload and its route are ready.

See installation for routing values and IAM integration for authentication.

docs.title: Persistent data
docs.text: Session files use PVCs; datasets use object storage; managed stores have their own volumes. Stopping a session keeps its home volume. See Operations for backups, retention, host security, and platform recovery.

docs.title: Install and configure Workspace
docs.text: Set up the shared services so teams can create workspaces, store data, and open sessions. Install the runtime, provider dependencies, composition packages, and API in that order. Use your platform’s GitOps process for a shared cluster.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
The platform needs Crossplane v2, Keycloak, object storage, an ingress controller, and a network plugin that enforces NetworkPolicy. Install the providers, functions, namespaced ProviderConfigs, and RBAC required by the selected Storage and Datalab packages.

Install Educates before creating Datalabs. The selected Educates base or ingress policies can also require Kyverno. Provider Datalab passes security settings to Educates; it does not create a complete host security policy.

Optional PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Qdrant stores need their operators installed first. The Provider Datalab installation guide lists these dependencies.

docs.title: Charts and API
docs.text:
This repository publishes charts in GitHub Packages:

Component What it installs Educates dependency chart The session runtime. Its input is dependencies/input.yaml. workspace-pipeline The Storage and Datalab configuration packages and one EnvironmentConfig.

Deploy the Workspace API and UI separately. Their source repository describes API configuration.

The pipeline uses skipDependencyResolution: true. It does not install the packages’ providers or functions. Check the exact package pins in pipeline/values.yaml; set storage.package and datalab.package to change them. A deployed environment can use different pins from this checkout.

From this checkout, save the values below as workspace-values.yaml, replace the example domains and network ranges, then install the pipeline:

helm upgrade --install workspace-pipeline ./pipeline \
  --namespace workspace --create-namespace \
  --values workspace-values.yaml

Check package health before creating a workspace:

kubectl get configurations.pkg.crossplane.io
kubectl get providers.pkg.crossplane.io
kubectl get functions.pkg.crossplane.io

docs.title: Educates runtime values
docs.text:
Educates provides the sessions that users open from their dashboard. These values configure its dependency chart. Set the same domain, ingress class, and certificate in the Datalab environment configuration so session links reach the correct runtime.

Key Purpose clusterIngressDomain Session domain, such as lab.example.org. clusterIngressClass Session ingress controller, such as apisix or nginx. tlsCertificateRef.name TLS Secret used for session hosts. tlsCertificateRef.namespace Namespace containing that TLS Secret.

docs.title: Pipeline environment values
docs.text: Use these values to give workspaces a common storage service, login system, network policy, and set of resource defaults. The keys are under environmentconfig in Helm values. The chart writes them into EnvironmentConfig.data. Empty default fields leave the provider to choose its fallback. The Datalab resource can override session resource and security defaults.

docs.title: Identity and routing
docs.text:
Key Purpose name EnvironmentConfig name. Chart default: datalab. iam.realm Keycloak realm. iam.namespace Keycloak namespace. iam.issuerURL Public realm URL used for login. iam.internalURL Realm URL reachable from the cluster. iam.extraAudiences Extra audiences for generated workspace-client tokens, such as workspace-api. ingress.enabled Use an Ingress for permanent Data access. Chart default: false. ingress.class, ingress.domain, ingress.secret Ingress controller, workspace domain, and TLS Secret name. The domain is also used by Data HTTPRoutes. ingress.annotations Ingress controller settings. httpRoute.enabled Use Gateway API for permanent Data access. Chart default: true. httpRoute.enableS3 Enable experimental S3 reads. Chart default: false. Requires HTTPRoute access. httpRoute.parentName, httpRoute.parentNamespace Gateway name and namespace. httpRoute.sectionName HTTPS listener that terminates TLS for Data. httpRoute.httpSectionName HTTP listener for the HTTPS redirect route.

For a permanent Data address, enable exactly one of ingress.enabled and httpRoute.enabled. With both disabled, Data uses session ingress. Enabling both stops reconciliation. The public load balancer must send traffic to the selected controller or Gateway.

docs.title: Storage and services
docs.text: Key Purpose storage.endpoint, storage.region Backing S3 endpoint and region. storage.forcePathStyle Path-style S3 addresses. Chart default: true; written as a string for the provider. storage.provider, storage.type Storage provider label and type. Type defaults to s3. storage.secretNamespace Namespace where Datalabs read their input storage Secrets. storage.lifecycle.schedule Storage lifecycle-job cron schedule. Provider fallback: 17 2 * * *. storageClasses.allowed Session PVC classes. An unlisted requested class falls back to the first entry. An empty list allows the requested or cluster default class. database.storageClassName, database.backupStorageClassName PostgreSQL data and backup classes, where supported by its operator. database.tlsRoute.parentName, database.tlsRoute.parentNamespace, database.tlsRoute.sectionName Gateway listener for optional external PostgreSQL access. mongodb.storageClassName, redis.storageClassName, qdrant.storageClassName Managed-store volume classes. Empty uses the cluster default. packages Extension packages for sessions.

docs.title: Resources and network
docs.text:
Key Purpose defaults.quota.memory Session memory. Provider fallback: 2Gi. defaults.quota.storage Session home-volume size. Provider fallback: 1Gi. defaults.quota.budget Educates resource budget. Provider fallback: medium. defaults.overallQuota.storage Total PVC requests in the Datalab environment namespace. Provider fallback: 100Gi. defaults.security.policy Pod security level: restricted, baseline, or privileged. Provider fallback: baseline. defaults.security.kubernetesAccess Supply a Kubernetes service account token. Provider fallback: true. defaults.security.kubernetesRole Namespace role: view, edit, or admin. Provider fallback: edit. defaults.security.externalEgress Enable the configured external rules. Provider fallback: true. network.externalEgressCIDRs External ranges allowed when external egress is enabled. An empty list creates no broad external allow rule. network.internalEgress Allowed namespaces, Pod selectors, and ports for internal services. network.internalIngress Allowed source namespaces, Pod selectors, and destination ports. Use targetPodSelector to select destination Pods. network.serviceCIDR, network.podCIDRs Cluster address ranges excluded from broad external rules. network.blacklistIPs Other ranges excluded from broad external rules, such as metadata endpoints. network.excludePolicies Generated NetworkPolicy names to omit.

See operational controls for how these settings affect sessions and Data.

docs.title: Example values
docs.text:
This example uses Gateway API for Data. Its HTTPS listener needs a certificate for *.lab.example.org and must accept routes from Datalab runtime namespaces. S3 reads also need support for HTTPRoute header regular expressions.

environmentconfig:
  name: datalab
  iam:
    realm: eoepca
    namespace: iam
    issuerURL: https://identity.example.org/realms/eoepca
    internalURL: http://keycloak-service.iam.svc/realms/eoepca
    extraAudiences:
      - workspace-api
  ingress:
    enabled: false
    class: apisix
    domain: lab.example.org
    secret: workspace-tls
  httpRoute:
    enabled: true
    enableS3: true
    parentName: public
    parentNamespace: gateway
    sectionName: workspaces-https
    httpSectionName: http
  storage:
    endpoint: https://s3.example.org
    forcePathStyle: true
    provider: Other
    region: us-east-1
    secretNamespace: workspace
    type: s3
  network:
    externalEgressCIDRs:
      - 0.0.0.0/0
      - ::/0
    internalEgress:
      - namespace: platform-services
        podSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: artifact-proxy
        ports:
          - protocol: TCP
            port: 443
    serviceCIDR: 10.43.0.0/16
    podCIDRs:
      - 10.42.0.0/16
    blacklistIPs:
      - 169.254.169.254/32
      - fd00:ec2::254/128
  defaults:
    overallQuota:
      storage: 100Gi
    security:
      policy: baseline
      kubernetesAccess: true
      kubernetesRole: edit
      externalEgress: true

httpRoute.enableS3 applies to all Data-enabled Datalabs in this environment. There is no per-Datalab S3 override. It controls the read-only Data endpoint; backing storage retains its own permissions.

For external PostgreSQL, configure a separate TLS-passthrough listener through database.tlsRoute. The Gateway controller must serve TLSRoute v1 and support direct PostgreSQL TLS with SNI.

docs.title: Select the environment
docs.text:
The chart creates one EnvironmentConfig named datalab by default. A manually created Storage resource can select it with:

metadata:
  labels:
    storages.pkg.internal/environment: datalab

Without an environment annotation or label, the MinIO composition selects storage. The Datalab key is datalabs.pkg.internal/environment. The Workspace API uses its PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT setting for resources it creates; its default is datalab.

docs.title: Verify the user path
docs.text:
Run the examples to check that users can reach the services you installed. Workspace Management creates a test workspace and checks storage and Data separately. This catches a workspace whose storage is ready but whose public address is not.

Use Vienna to check public downloads and authenticated S3 access. Use STAC registration to check service-account uploads, registry transfers, and STAC APIs in a session vCluster.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Create a workspace for a team, publish satellite images, and make the results available to other people and applications. The examples check that readers get the same bytes you uploaded and that the catalogue describes the published files.

Start with Workspace Management if you need a test workspace. Then choose Vienna for public and S3 downloads, or STAC registration for an automated upload and search APIs. The notebook guide helps you choose. You can use the same workspace for all three if it has the services listed below.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
These examples use eoepca-demo. The repository includes public service settings in eoepca-demo.env and a three-Item sample in docs/catalog.v1.parquet.

Requirement Used for alice and oscar accounts Alice owns the workspace; Oscar has the workspace-api platform admin role and creates it. Storage and a permanent Data address Upload files, browse public shares, and download data. Data S3 endpoint enabled Run the authenticated S3 and AWS CLI steps. Datalab with vCluster and registry Run the STAC registration notebook.

An operator sets up the accounts and roles and installs Workspace. For another deployment, change the service settings and account names.

docs.title: 1. Create a workspace
docs.text:
From the repository root:

uv sync
uv run jupyter lab docs/workspace-management.ipynb

Run Workspace Management. Sign in as Alice with device login, then as Oscar when the notebook asks for an administrator.

The notebook creates ws-test-<UTC timestamp>, waits for storage, and refreshes Alice’s token to load her workspace roles. Copy the printed workspace name for the other notebooks.

The API returns a name, for example:

{"name": "ws-test-20261024071434"}

The dashboard address is WORKSPACE_API_ENDPOINT/<workspace-name>. The API adds the configured ws- prefix to the preferred name.

docs.title: 2. Open the workspace
docs.text:
Open the dashboard link as Alice. It shows the storage connection and available sessions. Open a Datalab session to use its editor, terminal, and Data tab.

In on-demand mode, opening a stopped session starts it. Storage and the permanent Data service can be available before the session starts. The notebook waits separately for storage and the public Data route.

Use Management → Sessions to check the default session:

Workspace Management uploads the sample catalogue and its available preview and thumbnail images. It checks each uploaded image through an expiring S3 link, then through a permanent public-share link. Both downloads must match the uploaded bytes.

docs.title: 3. Publish and read satellite images
docs.text:
Open Vienna imagery with STAC and S3 and enter the workspace name from step 1.

Use this example to publish images that other people can inspect and download. The catalogue describes each cropped image, so a reader can find its date, area, and files. The notebook:

  1. Crops three Sentinel-2 images over Vienna and creates previews.
  2. Uploads those files and a STAC GeoParquet catalogue.
  3. Reads the published STAC items and public image links.
  4. Uses device login for authenticated S3 reads and the AWS CLI.
  5. Checks a byte-range read and compares download checksums.

Existing objects with matching checksums are kept. A different file at the same key stops the upload.

Open /share/public/ on the Data hostname to browse the published files:

docs.title: 4. Publish, relocate, and serve STAC data
docs.text:
Start the target workspace’s Datalab session. Open Register STAC metadata and enter its workspace name when asked. The default is ws-alice. To use the test workspace from step 1, change the name and use that workspace’s OAuth client and registry credentials.

The example has three flows. Flow 1 prepares three recent usable Sentinel-5P cloud fraction observations from the DLR GeoService STAC endpoint for use around Vienna. Portolan describes the clips and uploads them under published/. A first vCluster STAC API demonstrates search through a port-forward. Flow 2 uses stacpkg relocation to copy the assets from published/ to public/ in the same workspace bucket and keeps the source files. The metadata then uses PackageR HTTP asset links. The transfers use storage credentials fetched through OAuth and the Workspace API.

PackageR serves the public catalogue dynamically through the existing Data service. Preview it in MoreGeo STAC Browser and update the first API with the public metadata. Flow 3 pushes a metadata package to the workspace OCI container registry as an artifact. A second API uses an init container to pull it by digest, so a team can deploy the same catalogue again. The notebook guide compares the views. The APIs need the session to stay running.

Each registration run selects three observations. It keeps older published data and shared catalogue entries. The notebooks leave the workspace, uploaded files, and OCI package available for inspection.

docs.title: 5. Work with a team
docs.text:
Use the management page to add members and manage bucket access. Members use the workspace’s storage identity. To use a bucket owned by another workspace, request access and have its owner approve the grant.

See Concepts for the access model and steps for managing members, bucket grants, and sessions.

docs.title: 6. Use managed services
docs.text:
A workspace can request PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, or Qdrant when the platform has the required operators. Use the Stores tab when these services are available. Their connection settings appear on the dashboard and in new Datalab sessions.

For operator configuration and application examples, see Add a managed service.

PARQUET_TYPE = "application/vnd.apache.parquet"

)
PROCESSING_SCHEMA = "https://stac-extensions.github.io/processing/v1.2.0/schema.json"


class EmptyClipError(ValueError):
    """The observation has no valid pixels in the requested area."""


def recent_clips(candidates, catalog_dir, collection_id, bbox, count=3):
    """Clip the latest usable observation per day from newest-first candidates."""
    products = []
    days = set()
    for item in candidates:
        if item.datetime is None or "cf" not in item.assets:
            continue
        day = item.datetime.date()
        if day in days:
            continue
        try:
            product = clip_items([item], catalog_dir, collection_id, bbox)[0]
        except EmptyClipError:
            continue
        products.append(product)
        days.add(day)
        if len(products) == count:
            return sorted(products, key=lambda product: product["source"].datetime)
    raise ValueError(f"Found {len(products)} usable observations; need {count}.")


def public_url(data_url: str, key: str) -> str:
    """Return a permanent download route for a key below public/."""
    path = PurePosixPath(key)
    if path.is_absolute() or ".." in path.parts or path.parts[:1] != ("public",):
        raise ValueError("The object key must be below public/.")
    relative = str(path.relative_to("public"))
    if relative == ".":
        raise ValueError("Set a file path below public/.")
    return (
        f"{require_https(data_url)}/api/public/share/public/"
        f"{quote(relative, safe='/')}?presign=true&followRedirect=true"
    )


def clip_items(source_items, catalog_dir: Path, collection_id: str, bbox):
    """Write COGs and previews on the source grid, with no resampling."""
    if len(bbox) != 4 or not (
        -180 <= bbox[0] < bbox[2] <= 180 and -90 <= bbox[1] < bbox[3] <= 90
    ):
        raise ValueError("Set a valid longitude and latitude bounding box.")
    products = []
    for item in source_items:
        item_id = f"{collection_id}-{item.datetime:%Y%m%d}"
        directory = catalog_dir / collection_id / item_id
        cog = directory / "cf.tif"
        raw = directory / "xyz.tif"
        with rasterio.Env(
            GDAL_DISABLE_READDIR_ON_OPEN="EMPTY_DIR",
            GDAL_HTTP_TIMEOUT="60",
            GDAL_HTTP_MAX_RETRY="2",
        ):
            with rasterio.open(item.assets["cf"].href) as source:
                if source.crs != rasterio.CRS.from_epsg(4326):
                    raise ValueError("This clip expects a source grid in EPSG:4326.")
                requested = from_bounds(*bbox, transform=source.transform)
                left, top = math.floor(requested.col_off), math.floor(requested.row_off)
                right = math.ceil(requested.col_off + requested.width)
                bottom = math.ceil(requested.row_off + requested.height)
                window = Window(left, top, right - left, bottom - top).intersection(
                    Window(0, 0, source.width, source.height)
                )
                values = source.read(1, window=window, masked=True)
                if not values.count():
                    raise EmptyClipError(f"The clip has no valid pixels: {item.id}")
                directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                profile = source.profile.copy()
                profile.update(
                    driver="GTiff",
                    width=int(window.width),
                    height=int(window.height),
                    transform=source.window_transform(window),
                )
                with rasterio.open(raw, "w", **profile) as target:
                    target.write(values.filled(source.nodata), 1)
                    target.set_band_description(1, "Radiometric cloud fraction")
                    target.update_tags(AREA_OR_POINT="Area")
                    target.update_tags(
                        1,
                        STATISTICS_MINIMUM=str(float(values.min())),
                        STATISTICS_MAXIMUM=str(float(values.max())),
                        STATISTICS_MEAN=str(float(values.mean())),
                        STATISTICS_STDDEV=str(float(values.std())),
                        STATISTICS_VALID_PERCENT=str(
                            100 * values.count() / values.size
                        ),
                    )
            copy_raster(raw, cog, driver="COG", compress="DEFLATE", blocksize=256)
        raw.unlink()
        with rasterio.open(cog) as result:
            np.testing.assert_array_equal(result.read(1, masked=True), values)
            bounds = list(result.bounds)
            shape = [result.height, result.width]
            if result.tags(ns="IMAGE_STRUCTURE").get("LAYOUT") != "COG":
                raise ValueError("The output is not a COG.")
        grey = (np.clip(values.filled(0), 0, 1) * 255).astype("uint8")
        alpha = (~np.ma.getmaskarray(values) * 255).astype("uint8")
        image = PILImage.fromarray(np.dstack([grey, grey, grey, alpha]))
        for filename, size in [("preview.png", 512), ("thumbnail.png", 128)]:
            factor = size / max(image.size)
            resized = image.resize(
                tuple(max(1, round(side * factor)) for side in image.size),
                PILImage.Resampling.NEAREST,
            )
            resized.save(directory / filename)
        products.append(
            {
                "id": item_id,
                "source": item,
                "directory": directory,
                "cog": cog,
                "bbox": bounds,
                "shape": shape,
                "valid_pixels": int(values.count()),
            }
        )
    if len({product["id"] for product in products}) != len(products):
        raise ValueError("Select one source observation per day.")
    return products


def portolan(catalog_dir: Path, *arguments: str, credentials=None):
    """Run the CLI with only the settings supplied for this operation."""
    executable = Path(sys.executable).with_name("portolan")
    if not executable.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError("Run uv sync to install Portolan.")
    environment = {
        "PATH": f"{executable.parent}:/usr/bin:/bin",
        "AWS_CONFIG_FILE": "/dev/null",
        "AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE": "/dev/null",
        "AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED": "true",
    }
    if credentials:
        environment.update(
            {
                "AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID": credentials["access"],
                "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY": credentials["secret"],
                "AWS_REGION": credentials["region"],
                "PORTOLAN_S3_ENDPOINT": require_https(credentials["endpoint"]),
                "PORTOLAN_S3_USE_SSL": "true",
            }
        )
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            [str(executable), *arguments],
            cwd=catalog_dir,
            env=environment,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=600,
        )
        if result.returncode:
            # CLI errors can contain storage URLs. Do not copy them into output.
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Portolan {arguments[0]} failed (exit {result.returncode})."
            )
        return result
    finally:
        environment.clear()


def prepare_catalog(catalog_dir: Path, collection_id: str, products, source_collection):
    """Let Portolan describe the files, then add source and processing details."""
    if not (catalog_dir / "catalog.json").exists():
        portolan(
            catalog_dir,
            "init",
            "--auto",
            "--id",
            collection_id,
            "--title",
            "Cloud fraction around Vienna",
            "--license",
            "CC-BY-4.0",
            "--description",
            "Three daily cloud-fraction rasters clipped around Vienna.",
        )
    for product in products:
        source = product["source"]
        portolan(
            catalog_dir,
            "add",
            str(product["directory"]),
            "--datetime",
            source.datetime.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
            "--no-thumbnails",
        )
        candidates = [
            path
            for path in product["directory"].glob("*.json")
            if json.loads(path.read_text()).get("type") == "Feature"
        ]
        if len(candidates) != 1:
            raise ValueError("Portolan must create one STAC Item for each daily clip.")
        item_path = candidates[0]
        document = json.loads(item_path.read_text())
        document["id"] = product["id"]
        properties = document["properties"]
        for key in (
            "datetime",
            "start_datetime",
            "end_datetime",
            "platform",
            "constellation",
            "instruments",
            "sci:doi",
        ):
            if key in source.properties:
                properties[key] = source.properties[key]
        properties.update(
            {
                "title": f"Vienna cloud fraction, {source.datetime:%d %B %Y}",
                "description": "A clip on the source grid. Values are not resampled.",
                "license": "CC-BY-4.0",
                "processing:level": "L3",
                "processing:lineage": f"Clipped from DLR Item {source.id} with Rasterio.",
            }
        )
        with rasterio.open(product["cog"]) as raster:
            properties["proj:code"] = raster.crs.to_string()
            properties["proj:shape"] = [raster.height, raster.width]
            properties["proj:transform"] = list(raster.transform)
            properties["proj:bbox"] = list(raster.bounds)
        if isinstance(properties.get("instruments"), str):
            properties["instruments"] = [properties["instruments"]]
        # These fields must describe the output, not the global source raster.
        if not np.allclose(document["bbox"], product["bbox"], atol=1e-8):
            raise ValueError("Portolan bounds differ from the clipped raster.")
        data_asset = next(
            asset
            for asset in document["assets"].values()
            if asset["href"].endswith("cf.tif")
        )
        data_asset["title"] = "Radiometric cloud fraction"
        data_asset["roles"] = ["data"]
        for band in data_asset.get("bands", data_asset.get("raster:bands", [])):
            band["unit"] = "1"
        for key, filename, role in [
            ("preview", "preview.png", "overview"),
            ("thumbnail", "thumbnail.png", "thumbnail"),
        ]:
            # Remove a companion entry if Portolan gave it a different key.
            document["assets"] = {
                name: asset
                for name, asset in document["assets"].items()
                if not asset["href"].endswith(filename)
            }
            document["assets"][key] = {
                "href": f"./{filename}",
                "type": "image/png",
                "roles": [role],
                "title": "Clipped cloud fraction",
                "file:size": (product["directory"] / filename).stat().st_size,
                "file:checksum": "1220" + sha256(product["directory"] / filename),
            }
        source_href = (
            "https://geoservice.dlr.de/eoc/ogc/stac/v1/collections/"
            f"{quote(source.collection_id, safe='')}/items/{quote(source.id, safe='')}"
        )
        document["links"] = [
            link for link in document["links"] if link["rel"] != "derived_from"
        ]
        document["links"].append(
            {"rel": "derived_from", "href": source_href, "type": "application/geo+json"}
        )
        document["stac_extensions"] = list(
            dict.fromkeys(
                document.get("stac_extensions", [])
                + [
                    PROCESSING_SCHEMA,
                    "https://stac-extensions.github.io/scientific/v1.0.0/schema.json",
                ]
            )
        )
        item_path.write_text(json.dumps(document, indent=2) + "\n")
        product["item_path"] = item_path
    collection_path = catalog_dir / collection_id / "collection.json"
    collection = json.loads(collection_path.read_text())
    collection.update(
        {
            "title": "Cloud fraction around Vienna",
            "license": "CC-BY-4.0",
            "description": "Three daily DLR cloud-fraction rasters clipped around Vienna.",
            "providers": source_collection.get("providers", []),
        }
    )
    collection["providers"] = copy.deepcopy(collection["providers"])
    for provider in collection["providers"]:
        if "processor" in provider.get("roles", []):
            provider["roles"] = list(dict.fromkeys(provider["roles"] + ["producer"]))
    # Grid coordinates are Item fields, not ranges of independent numbers.
    for key in ("proj:bbox", "proj:shape", "proj:transform"):
        collection.get("summaries", {}).pop(key, None)
    collection["extent"] = pystac.Extent.from_items(
        [
            pystac.Item.from_dict(json.loads(p["item_path"].read_text()))
            for p in products
        ]
    ).to_dict()
    source_url = next(
        link["href"] for link in source_collection["links"] if link["rel"] == "self"
    )
    updated = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
    collection["updated"] = updated
    collection["links"] = [link for link in collection["links"] if link["rel"] != "via"]
    collection["links"].append({"rel": "via", "href": source_url, "type": "text/html"})
    # Give the collection a preview from the clipped data.
    collection.setdefault("assets", {})["thumbnail"] = {
        "href": f"./{products[0]['id']}/thumbnail.png",
        "type": "image/png",
        "roles": ["thumbnail"],
        "file:size": (products[0]["directory"] / "thumbnail.png").stat().st_size,
        "file:checksum": "1220" + sha256(products[0]["directory"] / "thumbnail.png"),
    }
    collection_path.write_text(json.dumps(collection, indent=2) + "\n")
    root_path = catalog_dir / "catalog.json"
    root = json.loads(root_path.read_text())
    root["updated"] = updated
    root["links"] = [link for link in root["links"] if link["rel"] != "via"]
    root["links"].append({"rel": "via", "href": source_url, "type": "text/html"})
    root_path.write_text(json.dumps(root, indent=2) + "\n")
    portolan(catalog_dir, "readme")
    portolan(catalog_dir, "stac-geoparquet", "--collection", collection_id)
    portolan(catalog_dir, "check", "--data-scope", "local")
    return collection_path


def publication_items(catalog_dir, products, bucket, prefix, data_url=None):
    """Set asset and document locations before the Portolan upload."""
    validate_prefix(prefix, "public" if data_url else "published")
    items = []
    files = {}
    for product in products:
        path = product["item_path"]
        document = json.loads(path.read_text())
        for asset in document["assets"].values():
            local = (path.parent / asset["href"]).resolve()
            relative = local.relative_to(catalog_dir.resolve()).as_posix()
            if not local.is_file():
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    "A STAC asset is missing from the local catalog."
                )
            key = f"{prefix}/{relative}"
            files[key] = local
            asset["href"] = f"s3://{bucket}/{key}"
            asset.pop("alternate", None)
            if data_url:
                asset["alternate"] = {"https": {"href": public_url(data_url, key)}}
            asset["file:size"] = local.stat().st_size
            # Multihash: sha2-256 code, digest length, digest.
            asset["file:checksum"] = "1220" + sha256(local)
        document["stac_extensions"] = list(
            dict.fromkeys(
                document.get("stac_extensions", [])
                + [
                    *([ALTERNATE_SCHEMA] if data_url else []),
                    "https://stac-extensions.github.io/file/v2.1.0/schema.json",
                ]
            )
        )
        # Keep the item table independent of its local directory.
        targets = {
            "self": path,
            "parent": catalog_dir / document["collection"] / "collection.json",
            "collection": catalog_dir / document["collection"] / "collection.json",
            "root": catalog_dir / "catalog.json",
        }
        document["links"] = [
            link for link in document["links"] if link["rel"] not in targets
        ]
        for rel, target in targets.items():
            key = f"{prefix}/{target.relative_to(catalog_dir).as_posix()}"
            document["links"].append(
                {
                    "rel": rel,
                    "href": public_url(data_url, key)
                    if data_url
                    else f"s3://{bucket}/{key}",
                    "type": "application/json",
                }
            )
        path.write_text(json.dumps(document, indent=2) + "\n")
        items.append(pystac.Item.from_dict(document))
    portolan(catalog_dir, "stac-geoparquet", "--collection", items[0].collection_id)
    return items, files


def write_parquet(items, destination: Path):
    table = stac_geoparquet.arrow.parse_stac_items_to_arrow(
        [
            item.to_dict(transform_hrefs=False)
            if isinstance(item, pystac.Item)
            else item
            for item in items
        ]
    ).read_all()
    stac_geoparquet.arrow.to_parquet(table, destination)


def read_parquet(path: Path):
    return list(stac_geoparquet.arrow.stac_table_to_items(pq.read_table(path)))


class WorkspacePublisher:
    """Get storage settings through OAuth, then run the workspace upload."""

    def __init__(self, issuer, api_url, workspace, client_id, client_secret):
        self.issuer = require_https(issuer)
        self.api_url = require_https(api_url)
        self.workspace = workspace
        self.client_id = client_id
        self._client_secret = client_secret
        self._session = requests.Session()
        self._session.trust_env = False
        self._credentials = None
        self._s3 = None

    def _json(self, method, url, **kwargs):
        try:
            response = self._session.request(
                method, url, timeout=30, allow_redirects=False, **kwargs
            )
            if response.status_code != 200:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"Workspace login or lookup failed (HTTP {response.status_code})."
                )
            return response.json()
        except requests.RequestException:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Cannot reach the workspace login or API service."
            ) from None

    def connect(self):
        if self._s3:
            self._s3.close()
            self._s3 = None
        if self._credentials:
            self._credentials.clear()
        discovery = self._json("GET", f"{self.issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration")
        if discovery.get("issuer") != self.issuer:
            raise ValueError("The discovery issuer differs from the configured issuer.")
        token = self._json(
            "POST",
            require_https(discovery["token_endpoint"]),
            data={
                "grant_type": "client_credentials",
                "client_id": self.client_id,
                "client_secret": self._client_secret,
            },
        )
        if (

        if not credentials or credentials["bucketname"] != self.workspace:
            raise PermissionError(
                "The client must have storage access to the target workspace."
            )

            "s3",

    def relocate(self, items, source_prefix, target_prefix, directory):
        """Run stacpkg relocation with supplied credentials and no saved logins."""
        from stacpkg.assets import asset_lock_table

        self.connect()
        sources, targets = relocation_locks(
            items,
            self.workspace,
            source_prefix,
            target_prefix,
            self._credentials["endpoint"],
        )
        pq.write_table(sources, directory / "published.assets.lock.parquet")
        pq.write_table(targets, directory / "public.destination.lock.parquet")
        expected = {
            (item.id, key): asset.extra_fields["file:checksum"]
            for item in items
            for key, asset in item.assets.items()
        }
        pending_sources, pending_targets, completed = [], [], []
        for source, target in zip(sources.to_pylist(), targets.to_pylist()):
            try:
                response = self._s3.get_object(Bucket=self.workspace, Key=target["key"])
            except ClientError as error:
                if error.response["Error"]["Code"] not in {
                    "404",
                    "NoSuchKey",
                    "NotFound",
                }:
                    raise
                pending_sources.append(source)
                pending_targets.append(target)
            else:
                digest = hashlib.sha256()
                with response["Body"] as body:
                    for chunk in iter(lambda: body.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
                        digest.update(chunk)
                if (
                    "1220" + digest.hexdigest()
                    != expected[(target["item_id"], target["asset_key"])]
                ):
                    raise ValueError(
                        "A public destination already has different content."
                    )
                completed.append(target)
        if pending_sources:
            destination = directory / "xyz-destination.lock.parquet"
            pq.write_table(asset_lock_table(pending_targets), destination)
            source_table = asset_lock_table(pending_sources)
            sink = pa.BufferOutputStream()
            with pa.ipc.new_stream(sink, source_table.schema) as writer:
                writer.write_table(source_table)
            environment = storage_environment(self._credentials)
            try:
                result = subprocess.run(
                    [
                        sys.executable,
                        "-m",
                        "stacpkg",
                        "asset-lock",
                        "relocate",
                        "--destination-lock",
                        str(destination),
                        "--no-overwrite",
                        "--max-workers",
                        "2",
                        "--memory-limit-bytes",
                        "128MiB",
                        "--chunk-size-bytes",
                        "4MiB",
                    ],
                    input=sink.getvalue().to_pybytes(),
                    env=environment,
                    capture_output=True,
                    timeout=600,
                )
            finally:
                environment.clear()
            if result.returncode:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    "stacpkg relocation failed. Check storage access and destination objects."
                )
            completed.extend(pa.ipc.open_stream(result.stdout).read_all().to_pylist())
        copied = asset_lock_table(completed)

        def locations(table):
            return {
                (row["item_id"], row["asset_key"]): (
                    row["store_type"],
                    row["store_container"],
                    row["key"],
                )
                for row in table.to_pylist()
            }

        if locations(copied) != locations(targets) or len(completed) != len(targets):
            raise ValueError("The relocation result differs from its destination plan.")
        pq.write_table(copied, directory / "public.assets.lock.parquet")
        return copied

    def upload_metadata(self, path, key):
        validate_prefix(key, "public")
        with path.open("rb") as body:
            self._s3.put_object(
                Bucket=self.workspace, Key=key, Body=body, ContentType=PARQUET_TYPE
            )

    def verify_assets(self, files):
        for key, local in files.items():
            response = self._s3.get_object(Bucket=self.workspace, Key=key)
            digest = hashlib.sha256()
            with response["Body"] as body:
                for chunk in iter(lambda: body.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
                    digest.update(chunk)
            if digest.hexdigest() != sha256(local):
                raise ValueError(f"Uploaded asset checksum differs: {key}")

    def update_public_catalog(self, items, directory):
        """Merge items and use an ETag condition to protect concurrent updates."""
        key = "public/catalog.parquet"
        existing = []
        etag = None
        try:
            response = self._s3.get_object(Bucket=self.workspace, Key=key)
        except ClientError as error:
            if error.response["Error"]["Code"] not in {"404", "NoSuchKey", "NotFound"}:
                raise
        else:
            etag = response["ETag"]
            previous = directory / "xyz-previous.parquet"
            with response["Body"] as body, previous.open("wb") as output:
                for chunk in iter(lambda: body.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
                    output.write(chunk)
            existing = read_parquet(previous)
        merged = {(item.get("collection"), item["id"]): item for item in existing}
        for item in items:
            document = item.to_dict(transform_hrefs=False)
            merged[(document.get("collection"), document["id"])] = document
        destination = directory / "catalog.parquet"
        write_parquet(list(merged.values()), destination)
        condition = {"IfMatch": etag} if etag else {"IfNoneMatch": "*"}
        with destination.open("rb") as body:
            self._s3.put_object(
                Bucket=self.workspace,
                Key=key,
                Body=body,
                ContentType=PARQUET_TYPE,
                **condition,
            )
        return destination

    def close(self):
        self._client_secret = None
        if self._credentials:
            self._credentials.clear()
        if self._s3:
            self._s3.close()
        self._session.close()

def use_registry_credentials(username, password):
    """Keep the pinned OCI client from loading a saved Docker login."""

    from oras.client import OrasClient
    import stacpkg.oci as stacpkg_oci

    def client(*, plain_http=False, insecure=False, auth_backend="basic"):
        if plain_http or insecure or auth_backend != "basic":
            raise ValueError(
                "Use HTTPS and Basic authentication for the workspace registry."
            )
        result = OrasClient(auth_backend="basic")
        result.auth.set_basic_auth(username, password)
        # stacpkg calls load_configs after creating its client. A nonempty
        # config stops ORAS from reading ~/.docker/config.json or its helpers.
        result.auth._auth_config = {"auths": {}}
        result.session.trust_env = False
        result.session.auth = (username, password)
        return result

    # stacpkg has no public client argument. Keep this adapter with its pin.
    stacpkg_oci._oras_client = client

def transfer_oci(package_dir, pulled_dir, host, repository, username, password):
    """Push, resolve the digest, and check a pull without a saved registry login."""
    require_https(f"https://{host}")
    tag = f"sha256-{sha256(package_dir / 'items.parquet')[:16]}"
    reference = f"{host}/{repository}:{tag}"
    environment = {
        "PATH": f"{Path(sys.executable).parent}:/usr/bin:/bin",
        "REGISTRY_USERNAME": username,
        "REGISTRY_PASSWORD": password,
    }

    script = (
        registry_client_code()
        + """

import sys
import time
import stacpkg.oci as registry

use_registry_credentials(os.environ["REGISTRY_USERNAME"], os.environ["REGISTRY_PASSWORD"])
operation, first, second = sys.argv[1:]
if operation == "push":
    registry.push_package(first, second, auth_backend="basic")
elif operation == "pull":
    registry.pull_package(first, second, auth_backend="basic")
else:
    raise ValueError("Select push or pull.")
"""
    )

    def command(operation, first, second):
        result = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-c", script, operation, str(first), str(second)],
            env=environment,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=600,
        )
        if result.returncode:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"OCI {operation} failed. Check the registry host and credentials."
            )

    try:
        command("push", package_dir, reference)
        with requests.Session() as session:
            session.trust_env = False
            response = session.head(
                f"https://{host}/v2/{repository}/manifests/{tag}",
                auth=(username, password),
                headers={"Accept": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json"},
                timeout=30,
                allow_redirects=False,
            )
            if response.status_code != 200:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"Cannot resolve the OCI tag (HTTP {response.status_code})."
                )
            digest = response.headers.get("Docker-Content-Digest", "")
            if not digest.startswith("sha256:") or len(digest) != 71:
                raise ValueError("The registry returned no SHA-256 manifest digest.")
        reference = f"{host}/{repository}@{digest}"
        command("pull", reference, pulled_dir)
        if package_hashes(package_dir) != package_hashes(pulled_dir):
            raise ValueError("The pulled package differs from the local package.")
        return reference
    finally:
        environment.clear()


def check_api(api_root, collection_id, expected_items, bbox):
    """Check collection, item, and search routes against the published Items."""
    with requests.Session() as session:
        session.trust_env = False

        def get(path, **params):
            response = session.get(f"{api_root}{path}", params=params, timeout=60)
            response.raise_for_status()
            return response.json()

        get("/conformance")
        get("/collections")
        path = f"/collections/{collection_id}"
        assert get(path)["id"] == collection_id
        features = get(f"{path}/items", limit=100)["features"]
        assert {f["id"] for f in features} == {i.id for i in expected_items}
        assert get(f"{path}/items/{expected_items[0].id}")["id"] == expected_items[0].id
        found = get(
            "/search",
            collections=collection_id,
            bbox=",".join(map(str, bbox)),
            limit=100,
        )["features"]
        assert {f["id"] for f in found} == {i.id for i in expected_items}
        assert not get("/search", collections=collection_id, bbox="-100,-50,-99,-49")[
            "features"
        ]
        assert not get(
            "/search",
            collections=collection_id,
            datetime="2000-01-01T00:00:00Z/2000-01-02T00:00:00Z",
        )["features"]
        response = session.post(
            f"{api_root}/search",
            json={
                "collections": [collection_id],
                "ids": [expected_items[0].id],
                "limit": 1,
            },
            timeout=60,
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        assert [f["id"] for f in response.json()["features"]] == [expected_items[0].id]
    check_items(features, expected_items)
    return features


def check_items(features, expected_items):
    expected = {item.id: item.to_dict(transform_hrefs=False) for item in expected_items}
    for feature in features:
        original = expected[feature["id"]]
        # Catalogs can write the same polygon with a different vertex order.
        assert shape(feature["geometry"]).equals(shape(original["geometry"]))
        assert feature["bbox"] == original["bbox"]
        for key in ("datetime", "start_datetime", "end_datetime"):
            assert datetime.fromisoformat(
                feature["properties"][key]
            ) == datetime.fromisoformat(original["properties"][key])
        for key in ("proj:shape", "proj:transform"):
            assert feature["properties"][key] == original["properties"][key]
        assert set(feature["assets"]) == set(original["assets"])
        for key, asset in feature["assets"].items():
            expected_asset = original["assets"][key]
            # Shared GeoParquet schemas can add null alternate fields.
            actual_alternates = {k: v for k, v in asset.get("alternate", {}).items() if v is not None}
            expected_alternates = {k: v for k, v in expected_asset.get("alternate", {}).items() if v is not None}
            assert actual_alternates == expected_alternates
            assert asset["file:checksum"] == expected_asset["file:checksum"]
            if asset["href"].startswith("s3://"):
                assert asset["href"] == expected_asset["href"]
            else:
                actual = urlsplit(asset["href"])
                public = urlsplit(
                    (expected_asset.get("alternate", {}).get("https") or {})
                    .get("href", expected_asset["href"])
                )
                assert (actual.scheme, actual.netloc, actual.path) == (
                    public.scheme,
                    public.netloc,
                    public.path,
                )


def check_public_assets(features, origin=None):
    """Read public files through fresh redirects and check their hashes and ranges."""
    with requests.Session() as session:
        session.trust_env = False
        for feature in features:
            for asset in feature["assets"].values():
                url = asset["href"]
                if not url.startswith("https://"):
                    url = asset["alternate"]["https"]["href"]
                headers = {"Origin": origin} if origin else {}
                response = session.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=120)
                if origin:
                    require_browser_cors(response, origin)
                if response.status_code != 200:
                    raise RuntimeError(
                        f"Public asset download failed (HTTP {response.status_code})."
                    )
                checksum = "1220" + hashlib.sha256(response.content).hexdigest()
                if checksum != asset["file:checksum"]:
                    raise ValueError("Public asset bytes differ from the local file.")
                response = session.get(
                    url, headers={**headers, "Range": "bytes=0-31"}, timeout=60
                )
                if origin:
                    require_browser_cors(response, origin)
                if response.status_code != 206 or len(response.content) != 32:
                    raise ValueError(
                        "The public asset does not support byte-range reads."
                    )
